task_completion.description: The OpenBCI GUI is open and visible on the screen.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The OpenBCI GUI window is visible, showing the 'Time Series' widget and EEG data streams.

task_completion.description: The GUI is in an active Synthetic EEG session with data streaming.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Start Data Stream' button is in its active state (usually showing 'Stop Data Stream') and moving waveforms are visible in the Time Series widget.

task_completion.description: The Notch filter setting is located within the Time Series widget.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The cursor or a dropdown menu is interacting with the 'Notch' button/label in the Time Series control bar.

task_completion.description: The Notch filter is successfully changed to 50 Hz.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The Notch filter button or dropdown in the Time Series widget explicitly displays '50 Hz'.

task_completion.description: A screenshot of the result is saved to the specified path.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A terminal command or file explorer window shows the creation of /tmp/notch_filter_result.png, or the final state of the GUI is captured as requested.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the GUI elements rather than just using terminal scripts to bypass the interface.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor moving to the Notch filter setting or the dropdown menu being expanded in the GUI.

integrity.description: The agent is using the actual OpenBCI GUI synthetic mode, not a static image or mockup.
integrity.visual_evidence: The waveforms in the Time Series widget show dynamic, non-repeating patterns characteristic of the OpenBCI synthetic generator.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply edit a configuration file via terminal to change the setting without opening the GUI.
integrity.visual_evidence: The visual state of the GUI changes from the default (usually 60 Hz) to 50 Hz during the trajectory.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The Notch filter setting is located in the top control bar of the 'Time Series' widget. The default value is typically 60 Hz; the target value is 50 Hz. The session must be in 'Synthetic' mode, and the data stream must be active (moving waveforms) when the screenshot is taken.
